about.title: Personal Injury Help in Banning, California
about.longDescription: Banning sits along the I-10 corridor, and that stretch of freeway — including the Eastbound and Westbound lanes and connecting streets like W Ramsey Street — sees a steady share of the area's collisions. In the most recent recorded year, Banning logged 104 injury collisions, 148 people hurt, and 3 traffic deaths. Many of these happen on Fridays between 6 and 8 p.m., when commuter and weekend traffic overlap near the freeway on- and off-ramps. If you or someone you love was hurt in one of these crashes, you probably have questions about medical bills, missed work, and what happens next. LawProactive is a free service — we are not a law firm — that connects injured people in Banning with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened and explain your options. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. We built this service because navigating a claim after an injury shouldn't add to your stress. Reaching out costs nothing and doesn't obligate you to anything.

whyChoose.title: What You Should Know Before You Wait

items.title: The clock is ticking
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it helps to act early.

items.title: Partial fault doesn't shut the door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the crash. Your compensation is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No cap on pain and suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. That means your claim isn't artificially limited by a statutory ceiling.

items.title: You don't pay unless there's a recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to you. Legal fees only come out of a settlement or award if your case succeeds.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Banning?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a claim. If your injury involved a government vehicle or entity, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking your situation sooner rather than later.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Banning?
items.answer: Public collision records show that Banning's crash counts are concentrated along the I-10 corridor, including both the Eastbound and Westbound lanes, as well as W Ramsey Street. These are simply the highest-volume roads by reported count, not a judgment about any location's safety.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, so being partly responsible doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault, but it isn't eliminated.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything upfront to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive's connection service is free, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover money. There's no cost or obligation to reach out and ask questions.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No, LawProactive is not a law firm. We're a free service that connects injured people in Banning and across Riverside County with independent personal injury attorneys who can evaluate their situation.
